integrity: Source model, likelihood factors, noninformative prior, posterior formula, and sampling-scheme distinction were inspected in the open full text. The parent distribution and related continuous Weibull posterior-propriety literature were compared. Uniform boundary asymptotics and a complete prior-measure Jacobian establish the theorem; the packaged numerical and symbolic checks provide independent reproducibility aids.
scientific_limitations: Applies to the unbounded shared-alpha Type-II and upper-record Bayesian priors as printed, not the mixed-record Bayesian scheme that conditions on alpha.
A proper or explicitly bounded prior changes the question and may yield a proper posterior.
Finite numerical integration can yield values despite a divergent full posterior normalizer, so numerical output alone does not identify an implementation.
title: The DAPW scale-invariant posterior is improper for every finite Type-II or upper-record dataset
